references.text: The same principle of impartiality in legal cases: one must neither favor the poor nor show partiality to the powerful, but judge fairly.
Moses urges judges not to show partiality in legal cases, but to treat small and great alike.
Prohibition against perverting justice or showing partiality; fairness must be followed.
Both verses specify the requirement of impartiality by warning against perverting justice for the benefit of the weak (the poor or the foreigner).
Both verses warn against letting social status (poverty) determine the outcome of a case, either through active oppression or misguided favoritism.
The proverb expands on the principle in the Exodus verse by showing that partiality is wrong both for the wicked and (implicitly) for the righteous, emphasizing the value of neutrality.
The proverb complements the Exodus verse by showing that injustice also occurs when one punishes the righteous, while Exodus warns against favoring the poor; both emphasize the need for objectivity.
